The '''1934–35 season''' was '''[[Real Madrid CF|Madrid Football Club]]'s''' [[List of Real Madrid CF seasons|33rd season]] in existence, and their [[La Liga records and statistics#All-time La Liga table|7th consecutive season]] in the [[La Liga|Primera División]]. The club also played in the [[Campeonato Regional Centro|Campeonato Regional Mancomunado]] (Joint Regional Championship) and the [[Copa del Rey|Copa del Presidente de la República]] (President of the Republic's Cup).

==Summary==
The club appointed Francisco Bru as coach for the season after a good streak of results last season. The squad was reinforced with several players, including forward [[Fernando Sañudo]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.marca.com/blogs/ni-mas-ni-menos/2015/03/01/fernando-sanudo-el-nino-de-los-pies-de.html|title=Fernando Sañudo, Golden Feet Boy|publisher=marca.com|date=1 March 2015|accessdate=24 December 2020|language=es}}</ref> Diz, Losada, Lopez, Rodrigo, Alonso and the first foreign transfer ever for the club, Hungarian goalkeeper [[:es:Gyula Alberti Kiszel|Gyula Alberti]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.as.com/misc/centenario/marzo/24.htm|title=Gyula Alberty Debut, first foreign footballer of Real Madrid|date=20 November 2013|accessdate=24 December 2020|publisher=as.com|language=es}}</ref> Despite a [[El Clásico#Biggest wins (5+ goals)|Clásico]] record for the biggest win in the league, a massive score of 8–2 on 3 February 1935 vs [[FC Barcelona]], including a poker of goals from "Golden Feet" Sañudo,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.mundodeportivo.com/20150203/futbol/la-mayor-goleada-en-un-clasico-de-liga-cumple-80-anos_54426813691.html|publisher=mundodeportivo.com|language=es|date=3 February 2015|accessdate=24 December 2020|author=Oscar Zarate|title=League Biggest Win 8-2 of Real Madrid against FC Barcelona 70 years ago}}</ref> the team ended up runners-up for the second consecutive year, this time losing the title by a single point to champions Betis Balompié.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://as.com/futbol/2015/04/27/album/1430142141_314592.html|title=1935: The First League for Betis|publisher=as.com|date=2 June 2015|accessdate=24 December 2020|language=es}}</ref>

Meanwhile, in the [[1935 Copa del Presidente de la República]], the team was defeated by [[Sevilla FC|Sevilla Football Club]] in the round of 16.
